item.title: Utsubo Park Rose Garden: A Green Oasis in the Business District — Guide
item.description: Utsubo Park is a slim, tree-lined green space threaded through the office towers of western Osaka, a favourite lunchtime escape for the district’s workers and a genuinely lovely city park. Its centrepiece is a rose garden of many hundreds of bushes, laid out formally around fountains, which comes into full bloom twice a year in a wash of colour and fragrance. The rest of the park mixes lawns, a tennis centre and broad tree-lined promenades, and it makes an easy, calm stop between the shops of nearby Shinsaibashi and the harbour.

item.title: Utsunomiya Castle Ruins & City: A Reconstructed Earthwork Park — Guide
item.description: Utsunomiya Castle was once a strategically important stronghold along the old Oshu Kaido road connecting Edo to northern Japan, home to a succession of feudal lords over several centuries. Most of the original structure was dismantled after the Meiji Restoration and the site suffered further damage in WWII bombing, but a modern restoration project has rebuilt sections of the earthwork ramparts, moat and a small viewing tower within what is now a landscaped city park, offering a glimpse of the castle’s former layout alongside walking paths and open green space.
